item.title: Federal policies a drag on Illinois economy, report finds
item.description: Illinois' economy will underperform the Midwest and the U.S. over the next year, due largely to the effects of federal policies, according to an economic forecast.

item.title: American Dream PILOT trustee sues mall developer, local government
item.description: The lawsuits argue that the owner of American Dream and East Rutherford, New Jersey, which sets tax assessments for the mall, colluded to depress its valuation.

item.title: Bond markets quiet to start the week
item.description: This week's expected elevated $12.6 billion in supply" "coincides with a recent uptick in secondary offerings … and may skim some froth from the market, particularly where spreads have hit one-year tights," said J.P. Morgan strategists led by Peter DeGroot.

item.title: Kansas local governments sign on to finance NFL Chiefs' move
item.description: The city of Olathe and the Unified Government of Wyandotte County-Kansas City, Kansas, signaled support for a state bond plan to move the team from Missouri.

item.title: Oregon lawmakers back Portland stadium renovation funding
item.description: An Oregon senator introduced legislation to create a $600 million Moda Center renovation package involving state, city and county government.

item.title: New Mexico eyes bond sales with passage of debt authorization
item.description: The state transportation commission expects to tap into $1.5 billion of revenue bond authorization with two deals totaling $350 million this year.

item.title: Housing bill advances
item.description: By an overwhelming bipartisan majority, the House advanced affordable housing legislation that includes a proposal that's expected to spur mortgage revenue bond issuance.

item.title: Gateway funds remain frozen as court battle plays out
item.description: Federal grants and loans account for $15 billion of the $16 billion Hudson Tunnels project.

item.title: S&P revises Denver's outlook to negative ahead of GO sale
item.description: The competitive bond sale comes after the triple-A-rated city received a negative outlook from S&P over the use of reserves to ease budget pressures.

item.title: Munis underperform USTs after retail sales data
item.description: Tuesday was a particularly heavy day of supply at an estimated $7.5 billion, per J.P. Morgan strategists.
